input.instructions: Create a compact, accurate blueprint for an 8-to-12-minute educational lesson with exactly ten sequential teaching beats. Do not write full narration. Create exactly three measurable learning objectives. For every beat, provide one distinct complete factual claim, a concrete example, a concise editable visual direction, and one or two exact supplied source IDs. End the claim, example, and visual direction with complete punctuation. Every cited source excerpt must directly support the claim; reuse at least two important technical terms from each cited excerpt so support can be checked locally. Do not invent course assignments, policies, measurements, datasets, instruction encodings, or product behavior that is absent from the supplied excerpts. Keep the claim, example, and visual direction compact; a deterministic local expander will produce the full narration. Sequence the beats from foundations through application and end with a practical analysis checklist. Use only the supplied source excerpts for factual claims. Every factual claim must cite one or more supplied source IDs. Narration must describe information that is essential to understand visuals. Do not imitate a named creator or invent sources.
input.prompt:
Topic: CSCI-521: Principles of Data Cleaning and Preparation. Create a representative course-foundations companion aligned to the official catalog description. It must teach durable concepts and problem-solving methods without claiming to replace the instructor's syllabus. Official catalog description: This course provides an introduction to the concepts and techniques used in preparing data for subsequent data mining. Topics include the knowledge discovery process; data exploration and its role; data extraction, cleaning, integration and transformation; handling numeric, unstructured, text, web, and other forms of data; and ethical issues underlying data preparation and mining. Data cleaning projects and a paper are required. Prerequisites: CSCI-320. Students may not take and receive credit for CSCI-521 and CSCI-721. If you have earned credit for CSCI-721 or you are currently enrolled in CSCI-721 you will not be permitted to enroll in CSCI-521. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

Source excerpts:

[neo4j-graph-data-modeling]
Property graph models represent domain entities as nodes. Relationships connect nodes and have a type and direction. Nodes and relationships can carry properties. Labels group nodes that play a similar domain role. A useful graph model begins from the questions the application must answer. Traversal patterns determine which relationships the application follows. Identity must be explicit when several records may describe the same entity. Constraints and indexes support data integrity and efficient lookup. Direction, cardinality, and update behavior are part of the model.

[postgresql-documentation]
Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types. Primary keys identify rows, while foreign keys express references between tables. Constraints reject states that violate declared data rules. Queries select, join, aggregate, insert, update, and delete data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected queries. Transactions group operations into an atomic unit of work. Isolation controls how concurrent transactions observe one another. Schema design separates entities and relationships, while normalization addresses update anomalies. Query planning and physical structures influence performance without changing logical query meaning.

beats.claim: CSCI-521 introduces the knowledge discovery process and establishes data cleaning as a prerequisite for effective data mining.
beats.example: Students will review the official course catalog to confirm that data cleaning projects and a paper are required for credit.
beats.title: Course Foundations and Scope
beats.visualDirection: Display the official course catalog excerpt highlighting the knowledge discovery process and required deliverables.

beats.claim: Data exploration is a critical phase that identifies patterns, anomalies, and quality issues before transformation.
beats.example: Instructor will demonstrate how exploratory data analysis reveals missing values and outliers in a sample dataset.
beats.title: Data Exploration and Its Role
beats.visualDirection: Show a split-screen comparison of raw data versus explored data highlighting identified anomalies.

beats.claim: Data extraction and cleaning involve removing irrelevant records, correcting errors, and standardizing formats.
beats.example: Students will practice extracting structured data from a CSV file and removing duplicate rows using standard cleaning techniques.
beats.title: Data Extraction and Cleaning
beats.visualDirection: Animate the step-by-step removal of duplicate rows and standardization of date formats in a spreadsheet.

beats.claim: Data integration combines multiple data sources, while transformation converts data into a consistent format for analysis.
beats.example: Instructor will demonstrate merging two relational tables and converting categorical variables into numeric codes.
beats.title: Data Integration and Transformation
beats.visualDirection: Display a before-and-after table showing merged columns and transformed categorical values.

beats.claim: Numeric data requires specific cleaning techniques such as imputation for missing values and normalization for scale consistency.
beats.example: Students will calculate the mean and median to impute missing numeric values and apply min-max normalization to a dataset.
beats.title: Handling Numeric Data
beats.visualDirection: Show a bar chart comparing raw numeric values versus normalized values ranging from 0 to 1.

beats.claim: Unstructured and text data require preprocessing steps like tokenization, stop-word removal, and stemming before analysis.
beats.example: Instructor will demonstrate converting a paragraph of text into a list of tokens and removing common stop words.
beats.title: Handling Unstructured and Text Data
beats.visualDirection: Display a word cloud transitioning from raw text to a cleaned token list with stop words highlighted.

beats.claim: Web data extraction involves parsing HTML, handling dynamic content, and managing rate limits to ensure data quality.
beats.example: Students will scrape a static webpage, parse the HTML structure, and extract structured records while respecting server rate limits.
beats.title: Handling Web Data
beats.visualDirection: Show a flowchart of the web scraping process from request to parsed JSON output.

beats.claim: Data integrity is maintained through constraints, indexes, and validation rules that enforce data quality standards.
beats.example: Instructor will demonstrate how primary keys and foreign keys prevent duplicate and orphaned records in a relational database.
beats.title: Data Integrity and Constraints
beats.visualDirection: Display a database schema diagram highlighting primary key and foreign key relationships.

beats.claim: Ethical considerations in data preparation include privacy protection, bias mitigation, and responsible data usage.
beats.example: Students will review a case study on anonymizing personal data and ensuring fair representation in cleaned datasets.
beats.title: Ethical Issues in Data Preparation
beats.visualDirection: Show a checklist of ethical guidelines for data preparation and mining.

beats.claim: A practical analysis checklist ensures all data cleaning steps are verified, documented, and aligned with course objectives.
beats.example: Students will complete a checklist verifying extraction accuracy, cleaning completeness, transformation consistency, and ethical compliance.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Display a printable checklist template with checkboxes for each verification step.

learningObjectives: Define the knowledge discovery process and explain how data cleaning serves as a foundational step for subsequent data mining.
Apply techniques for data extraction, cleaning, integration, and transformation across numeric, unstructured, text, and web data formats.
Evaluate ethical considerations in data preparation and mining, ensuring compliance with data integrity and privacy standards.
